title: HTML Template: Importing document fragment
body:
**Use case:**

A web site using a common header and footer across all of its web pages, wishing browsers would cache them instead of requesting them every time.  The pages could be cached templates as well, containing a list of cached templates.  These templates could also contain 'dynamic' templates, which would only contains the dynamic data - where a cached version shouldn't be used - that the user really needs to fetch again when refreshing a web page.  It shouldn't require Javascript.  The objective being a reduction in web traffic and ease of maintenance for the webmaster, without the need of a server-side scripting language.

**Example:**

A way to achieve this goal with the actual standard and a little bit of Javascript is presented in this [repository](https://github.com/maherbo/HTML-Template-Caching).

The major problem with this method (apart from the use of Javascript) is the use of IFRAME elements, which require the construction of an entire document for each IFRAME.  The requested template file should be recognized as a document fragment only.

**Solution:**

This process could be triggered by the simple addition of an attribute 'src' on any element that the content model is not defined as nothing or embedded content.

When such an element has a 'src' attribute, any children node must be ignored.  Its content must be instead retrieved from the source file and added to the document tree as its children.  If the 'src' attribute is added or changed, the element content is changed to the new source file content.  If the 'src' attribute is removed, the actual content is kept.
